subject: history_social
passage: According to the usual account, in late 1946 or early 1947 Bedouin shepherds searching for a stray goat near Qumran, on the northwestern shore of the Dead Sea, entered a cave and found clay jars holding ancient scrolls. Over the next decade, archaeologists and local searchers recovered fragments of roughly nine hundred manuscripts from eleven caves in the area. The oldest of these texts, written mostly in Hebrew and Aramaic on parchment and papyrus, ______ to the third century BCE, about a thousand years earlier than most previously known manuscripts of the Hebrew Bible.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: The subject of the last sentence is "The oldest of these texts"; "written mostly in Hebrew and Aramaic on parchment and papyrus" is a description of them, not a verb. The sentence still needs a main verb, so the blank must be a finite verb: "date."
explanation.A: Correct. "Date" is a finite verb that gives the subject "The oldest of these texts" its main verb.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Dating" is a participle, so the sentence would have no main verb.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Having dated" is a participle phrase, so the sentence would still lack a main verb.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "To date" is an infinitive, which cannot serve as the main verb of a sentence.
